slots.title: Japan GDP shrinks for first time in four quarters
slots.body:
Japan’s economy contracted on an annualized basis in the July–September quarter — the first decline in four quarters — as consumption faltered.

That read landed alongside a weaker session in Tokyo: the Nikkei 225 finished down 1.7% at 60,104.35.

Energy-driven inflation has been cited in coverage as a drag on consumer sentiment during the period.

How much does Japan’s growth print change how you read Asia’s year-end setup?

slots.title: US close — Nov. 15, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite finished down 0.9% at 25,136.27, a 229.82-point decline from the prior close, with a session range between 25,423.09 and 24,872.41.

The S&P 500 closed down 0.4% at 7,561.67, off 30.73 points, after trading between 7,621.78 and 7,499.40.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was the outlier among major U.S. benchmarks, up 0.1% at 52,347.55, while the Russell 2000 slipped 0.3% to 2,790.49.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 3.2% to 19.30, with an intraday high of 20.92, as equity benchmarks mixed and tech weighed on the growth-heavy indexes.

Semiconductor-related megacaps recorded some of the largest dollar-weighted moves: Advanced Micro Devices fell 8.8% to $534.06 on volume of about 49.4 million shares, with a low of $520.01; NVIDIA closed down 2.0% at $162.85; Taiwan Semiconductor fell 1.7% to $398.73.
Direxion’s 3x bull semiconductor ETF ($SOXL) lost 11.0% to $58.32, while the 3x bear counterpart ($SOXS) gained 11.1% to $50.78.

Meta Platforms rose 2.9% to $641.69, Alphabet Class C shares fell 1.0% to $292.52, Tesla slipped 1.8% to $390.22, and Apple inched up 0.4% to $356.27 with a session high of $360.83 in the data.

Defensive and consumer-oriented megacaps helped support the Dow: Johnson & Johnson gained 0.8% to $285.75, Costco Wholesale rose 1.3% to $1,106.21 with a high matching its 52-week peak of $1,109.50, Eli Lilly added 1.3% to $1,443.50, and Chevron climbed 1.6% to $219.89.

Payment networks Visa and Mastercard each closed up 1.3%, at $425.76 and $661.19 respectively, on the same day the Nasdaq fell.

Energy-linked exposure was mixed versus crude: Exxon Mobil rose 0.5% to $170.59 while the United States Oil Fund ETF fell 0.3% to $145.58; Brent crude in the cross-asset set was down 0.6% at $95.27.

Gold futures slipped 0.2% to $3,877.00; the dollar-bullish ETF proxy (UUP) rose 0.3% to $29.50; Bitcoin traded down 0.8% at $64,824.27.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-11-13) showed the 10-year at 5.2% and the 2s10s spread at 0.27 percentage points—context for rates on the tape, not a same-day print in this file.

Overseas indexes in the bundle for the surrounding window included the Nikkei 225 down 1.8% at 60,066.52, while the FTSE 100 rose 0.4% and the Hang Seng gained 0.7%; WSJ coverage described Asian equity weakness in connection with the U.S. chip-maker selloff.

No major U.S. economic releases or earnings actuals were listed in the injected calendar for this session; the economic and earnings calendar arrays were empty, and sector performance breakdowns were not provided in the data.

Among lighter, high-percent movers, Modine Manufacturing ($MOD) rose 27.9% to $135.66 and Newsmax ($NMAX) gained 31.4% to $9.58 on the liquid-gainers list, separate from the megacap narrative that dominated index direction.
